provenance.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. EDIT reference image 1, the existing adult male House Sparrow. Image 2 is the original four-bird style collection. Image 3 is the preferred Woodpigeon refinement showing clearer graphic organisation.
Produce ONE finished landscape 4:3 image. This is a narrow graphic refinement of the House Sparrow, preserving its current pose, size, anatomy, facing right, mineral-blue and sage background shapes, paper, ink support, and exact handwritten name "House sparrow".
CHANGE ONLY THE DRAWING TREATMENT: Group the cream cheek, grey/buff belly and chestnut shoulder into slightly clearer, deliberately shaped pigment areas. Keep selected fine coloured-pencil feather detail within those areas, but let some body passages be calmer. Give the overlapping coverts and shoulder feather groups a clearer rhythm, with selective dark separations and tapered pale edges. Keep the existing wing's excellent long fine shaft drawing. Preserve detailed craftsmanship without evenly scratching every surface to the same intensity. Let a few varied dark contours and feather tips feel more drawn and intentional; no universal heavy outlines, extra glossy shading or gold ornament sprinkled over everything.
IDENTITY INVARIANTS: adult male House Sparrow (Passer domesticus), grey crown, chestnut sides of the head and nape, pale cheek without a black cheek spot, black throat/bib, stout short conical bill, chestnut back with dark streaking, buff-grey underside, natural brown-pink legs. Do not change it into a Tree Sparrow. Do not enlarge the eye, chest, bill, head, feet or tail.
Keep the existing ivory paper, translucent underpainting, rich print-like pigment, dry-grain texture and sharp fine linework. More deliberate graphic shapes with species fidelity, not a simplified cartoon.
Only text "House sparrow". No status, scenery, accessory, fact, extra text or watermark.
